metadata.purpose: Section briefs for VoltVision Challenge 2026 manuscript

key_points: Malaysia accelerating EV transition driven by policy incentives, expanding infrastructure, private investment
EV registrations doubled in 2025 (44,813 units, 5.2% TIV penetration)
Government targets: 20% EV share by 2030, 80% by 2050
ASEAN region emerging as global EV leader, Malaysia trails peers
Significant challenges remain: rising costs, infrastructure gaps, limited historical data, evolving risk dynamics
Insurance industry faces unique EV risks: battery cost concentration, repair complexity, total loss dynamics
Charging infrastructure at 56% of target, urban-centric distribution
Repair ecosystem immature: limited certified workshops, technician shortage
No Malaysian-specific EV claims frequency/severity data published
Insurance pricing uses ICE-based models with unknown adequacy
Consumer awareness of EV-specific insurance needs low (<20% flood cover)
End-of-life battery management framework still developing
JPJ registration data (official, comprehensive)
MAA industry data (member-based, excludes some brands)
PIAM industry insights (insurance-specific)
MEVnet charging infrastructure dashboard
Research house reports (Kenanga, Hong Leong, MBSB)
Academic literature (UiTM, MDPI)
Comparative analysis: Malaysia vs ASEAN peers
Trend analysis: 2021-2026 registration trajectory
Stakeholder mapping: insurers, OEMs, regulators, consumers
Risk assessment: battery, repair, infrastructure, policy
China EV data as proxy for Malaysian claims patterns (PIAM approach)
ASEAN peer data for benchmarking where local data unavailable
Reasonable assumptions clearly stated per playbook requirements

T1_pricing: Battery = 30-50% of vehicle value, concentrated risk
Motor segment underwriting loss RM289.3M, combined ratio 103%
ADAS calibration costs RM5k-15k per incident
T2_solutions: Zurich Z-Driver EV Protect: RM120 add-on validated
Great Eastern GREAT EV: battery allowance, wall charger
Takaful options emerging for Shariah-compliant market
T3_ecosystem: Charging: 5,624 installed, DC exceeded target, AC lagging
Repair: 7/10 independent workshops decline EV work

points: CBU tax expiry: momentum continues (Proton e.MAS 5) vs slowdown forecast
MAA vs JPJ data: true EV penetration uncertain
Battery lifespan: 8-10 years vs longer for LFP chemistry
No published Malaysian EV claims frequency/severity data
limitations.implications: Research gaps identified as future work areas

points: Battery passport implementation and data sharing
